'''Sandy Wible Inexpensive Tournament Winning Deck!''' is a [[Light]] constructed list published on Decipher Deck Designs.

== Deck info ==
* '''Player:''' [[Sandy Wible]]
* '''Published:''' December 1997 (Decipher Deck Designs)
* '''Format:''' [[Premiere - Cloud City]]
* '''Side:''' [[Light]]
* '''Starting Card:''' {{CardLink|Yavin 4: Jungle|Premiere-L-yavin4jungle.gif}}
* '''Strategy:''' Inexpensive Tournament Winning Deck!
* '''GEMP Importable deck:''' [[Media:PCC Inexpensive Tournament Winning Deck!.txt |Download]]

== Introduction ==

Here is a dark deck that I used to win a recent tournament. It uses many commons, and few expensive cards. Even the few medium-value cards used may be easily exchanged for common and uncommon cards, as the strength of these decks is not in individual cards but rather in the strategy used and in cunning implementation. Enjoy!

== Strategy ==

Be very cagey with deploying either Mos Eisley or the Holotable at the start of the game. Imperial Justice is a very strong card in the first few turns. Holding back on deploying new locations can really put the whammy on an opponent by denying Force generation.

Starting with the Holotable as opening location is a very strong play, but works against the Imperial Justice ploy. If the opponent has little to no dejariks, then this is a free Force drain all game. If the opponent has a dejarik deck, then it is likely that both of you will be starting with the holosites and thus it will deny him the opportunity to start with it. Both must choose another starting location and reshuffle.

If a Ghhhk is in the opening hand, definitely put a Stormtrooper in the Jungle on the first turn. Only deploy new locations if you have enough characters in hand, or Ghhhks, to cover potential counterattacks.

Mosep and the Limited Resources are opposing strategies. Use one or the other, but probably not both. Mosep should be saved and deployed late in the game, when the opponent has few cards in Life Force but many in hand, and thus will take a big blow via Force drain. He will have few cards to activate to deploy cards in hand, and will be hampered late in the game. Plus, it becomes possible to defeat the opponent more quickly, reducing the available cards he can lose to Force drain.

Limited Resources may be played, several at a time, once the opponent reduces down to two or less cards. Watch for Grimtaash, and put doubles of Limited Resources back via Traffic Control, if this danger seems possible early in the game. You will probably draw them again later, and will still have one in hand to use.

Undercover and U-3PO are not to be ignored. Save spies to block Force drains elsewhere on the table.
